body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Buying the perfect USB-C charger may look simple at first, but the reality is full of potential gotchas. If you’ve ever reached for your cable only to find that your device is still charging hours later, you’re certainly not alone. In one sense, USB-C and USB Power Delivery were supposed to solve this mess. The universal connector and new regulations, such as those introduced in the EU, were designed to ensure that one charger could support everything. In some ways, that has been a success: USB-C can now be found on almost every phone, tablet, laptop, and more. However, the difference between something that technically works and something that works optimally can still be surprisingly wide.

title: Maybe the FCC was onto something: These routers are phoning home to China with a secret backdoor
summary: Of course, because they predate the ban, the FCC continues to permit their sale.
body: TL;DR A new report details a massive security flaw in Zbtlink-made routers. The routers are programmed to ping a hard-coded list of servers, traced back to China. Once connected, the routers grant full root access — no authentication required. This past spring, the FCC announced a sweeping ban on new foreign-made routers — like the kind you use to get online with your ISP and connect all your devices to Wi-Fi. This was all done in the name of national security, but just how real of a threat do routers pose? The discovery of a new security vulnerability in some Chinese-made routers may have you looking at the FCC’s action in a slightly more sympathetic light. Jacob Baines at VulnCheck shares his analysis of routers made by Zbtlink, sold under both that and Wiflyer branding. While neither are huge names in the router space, they’re still sold through US retailers like Amazon , and have been around for years — so, plenty of time for these devices to make some inroads on the market.

Rather than the usual two foldables — a Flip and a Fold — Samsung’s released three, including two book-style Z Fold phones in different aspect ratios. People have seemed excited about the new, wider form factor (the marginally less premium of the two) since before the phones were released , and now a survey Android Authority ‘s been running has confirmed that vibe. In a poll we’ve been running since late July, we asked readers which of the two Z Fold 8 phones they’d be more likely to buy. There were four options: the wide Z Fold 8; the narrow, higher-end Z Fold 8 Ultra; a response for people who hadn’t decided yet; and one for folks who just aren’t interested. title: Signal finally makes using multiple Android devices much easier
summary: You no longer have to choose which phone gets to keep your Signal chats.
body: TL;DR Signal now lets you link another Android phone or tablet to your existing account. You can optionally transfer your message history and the last 45 days of media. The update also redesigns Android tablet and foldable layout, ditching legacy single-screen navigation. For years, one of Signal’s biggest pain points when compared to other messaging apps wasn’t encryption, voice calls, or missing features. It was the awkward experience of moving between devices. If you wanted to use a second Android phone or tablet, you were largely out of luck. That finally changes with the latest update. Signal has announced a major expansion of its linked devices feature, allowing users to connect another Android phone or Android tablet to their existing account. The feature arrives in Signal Android v8.20, while Signal iOS v8.22 similarly lets iPhone users link another iPhone alongside existing iPad support.

summary: What's the state of play with Android 17 on the Pixel 10?
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority The Pixel 10 series may be Google’s best phones yet, but gamers got the short end of the stick. The Tensor G5 marked Google’s switch away from Arm’s Mali GPUs in favor of Imagination Technologies’ PowerVR architecture — specifically the mid-range, already aging DXT-48-1536. With the Pixel 11 launch approaching, one question keeps nagging at me: will history repeat itself? Rumors suggest the Tensor G6 will use another modest PowerVR GPU, the CXTP-48-1536. If Google’s recent trajectory is anything to go by, the Pixel 11 could fall even further behind rival flagship GPUs.

title: Google may finally fix a major frustration with Android’s Photo Picker
summary: Code in Android 17 QPR 2 Beta 2 reveals plans for a built-in media editor, which could save users from tedious app switching.
body: Credit: Mishaal Rahman / Android Authority TL;DR Google is laying the groundwork to add a built-in media editor directly to the Android Photo Picker. Code in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 2 reveals an “EditFeature” class designed as a pop-up dialog for quick edits like cropping and marking. Because the Photo Picker updates via Google Play System Updates, this feature can roll out independently of a full OS update. Android’s Photo Picker is a system component that provides third-party apps with a browsable interface for accessing media library content. It’s a massive leap forward for user privacy, as it allows users to share specific photos and videos with third-party apps without giving them access to their full media library. For app developers, it saves them the effort of building this interface themselves. Google has refocused its efforts on improving the Android Photo Picker, as we’ve spotted features like a camera shortcut in the works.
